title: Modi Says Direct Benefit Transfers Saved Rs 5 Lakh Crore From Leakage
excerpt: At the 10th India Mobile Congress, the Prime Minister said Rs 50 lakh crore has flowed directly to beneficiaries' bank accounts, calling the mobile phone the backbone of governance.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi said India's Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system has saved nearly Rs 5 lakh crore from falling into "wrong hands," speaking at the 10th India Mobile Congress in New Delhi.
  • Modi said Rs 50 lakh crore has been transferred directly to beneficiaries' bank accounts through mobile-based DBT, while over Rs 4 lakh crore has reached farmers under PM-KISAN.
  • Reader utility: DBT runs on Aadhaar-linked bank accounts — NRIs with family in India should make sure relatives' Aadhaar-bank seeding is current, since subsidies now reach beneficiaries directly with no middlemen.
  • Modi also called the mobile phone "both a gaming console and a creation studio," citing 500 million Indians connected to gaming and 5G coverage in every district.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Thursday that India's Direct Benefit Transfer system has saved nearly Rs 5 lakh crore from falling into "wrong hands," presenting the country's mobile-first welfare delivery as one of the world's largest anti-leakage exercises. Speaking at the inauguration of the 10th India Mobile Congress (IMC 2026) at Yashobhoomi in New Delhi, Modi said Rs 50 lakh crore has been transferred directly into beneficiaries' bank accounts through the DBT framework.

"India's digital infrastructure has become a key instrument of governance and delivery of public services," Modi said, noting that direct transfers eliminated the layers of middlemen that once siphoned off welfare funds. He said the mobile phone is "no longer merely a means of communication or chatting" but the backbone of how the state reaches its citizens.

The numbers behind the DBT machine

The Rs 5 lakh crore savings figure is the latest government estimate of cumulative leakages plugged since DBT was scaled up after 2014. The mechanism is straightforward: subsidies and scheme payments land directly in Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts of verified beneficiaries. Officials have previously said about Rs 3.48 lakh crore was saved by March 2023, with roughly Rs 64,000 crore saved each year as fake and duplicate beneficiaries were purged. The biggest savings came from deleting 4.15 crore duplicate or inactive LPG connections (Rs 73,443 crore) and 7.1 lakh fake MGNREGA job cards in a single year (Rs 42,534 crore), according to government data cited by IANS.

Modi also said more than Rs 4 lakh crore has been paid to farmers under the PM-KISAN income-support scheme.

A decade of digital infrastructure

IMC, now in its tenth edition, is organised by the Department of Telecommunications and the Cellular Operators Association of India; this year's theme is "Scale Without Boundaries." Modi reminded the audience that 5G was launched at IMC 2022 — today, he said, it reaches every district in the country on more than 5.5 lakh base stations, and mobile internet speeds are roughly ten times faster than in 2022.

He also reached for a less expected audience — gamers. The phone, Modi said, has "today become both a Gaming console and a creation studio," estimating that more than 500 million Indians are connected to gaming in some form, with young players and creators concentrated in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. The remark came without any new esports scheme, but signalled the government counts gaming as a mainstream sector of the mobile economy.

Impact and analysis

The DBT figure is a governance-efficiency argument as much as a financial one. At roughly $60 billion, the claimed savings dwarf the welfare budgets of most countries, and the India Stack model of Aadhaar, UPI and DBT has become a reference point for countries trying to cut welfare leakage. The caveats are familiar: the savings are government estimates, not independently audited, and economists have long debated how much represents genuine fraud versus beneficiaries who failed Aadhaar authentication for administrative reasons. Exclusion errors remain the system's most persistent criticism.

"The mobile phone is no longer merely a means of communication or chatting. In India, the mobile phone has today become both a Gaming console and a creation studio."

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India

Diaspora angle

For NRIs, the DBT story matters most at the household level: parents and relatives back home now receive subsidies, pensions and PM-KISAN payments directly in their bank accounts, tied to Aadhaar-bank seeding. Anyone managing family affairs in India should check that elderly relatives' Aadhaar is linked and seeded to the right account — failed seeding remains the most common reason a legitimate beneficiary stops receiving money. Modi also called for a global framework to tackle cyber frauds and deepfakes, per The Hindu — relevant as 12 percent of Indians now report being scammed in the past year.

What's next

IMC 2026 runs through the weekend, with operators and startups showcasing 6G research, satellite connectivity and AI infrastructure. Watch for whether the DBT savings claim translates into new digital-infrastructure partnerships — and for the deepfake framework Modi floated, which would put India at the centre of an emerging global regulatory conversation.
